ICYMI O/N

IRAN:

Iran’s negotiators will arrive in Islamabad Thursday night for “serious talks” with the U.S. despite Israel’s continued ground operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon, Iran’s envoy to Pakistan, Reza Amiri Moghadam, said on social media. However, note the post has since been deleted. (WSJ)

US President Trump late Wednesday issued a new warning as a cease-fire with Iran got off to a shaky beginning, saying the “shootin’ ” would start again if the “REAL AGREEMENT” is not fully complied with, adding that that would be “highly unlikely”. (Truth Social)

Just four ships were identified passing through the strait on Wednesday, down from 11 on Tuesday, according to ship tracking data. (FT)

WSJ reports Trump’s declaration of “total victory” in Iran left some close allies and several senior aides worried Wednesday that he is overstating what is a fragile cease-fire with Tehran. The report notes Iran still has military capabilities despite the heavy damage, noting the IRGC still retains dozens of small boats that can threaten ships in the Strait. (WSJ)

Hezbollah said early Thursday it had targeted northern Israel with a rocket salvo, in response to what it described as an Israeli violation of the cease-fire. (WSJ)

Israel is seizing more territory from its neighbours in preparation for a long, drawn-out conflict across the Middle East. Israel's creation of "buffer zones" in Gaza, Syria and now Lebanon reflects a strategic shift after the attacks of October 7, 2023, one that puts the country in a semi-permanent state of war, six Israeli military and defence officials told Reuters. (RTRS)

The US wants specific commitments from European allies on their pledge to help secure the Strait of Hormuz after the fighting in Iran stops, requesting that the countries present concrete plans to ensure navigation through the waterway within days, according to a senior NATO official cited by Bloomberg. (BBG)

The White House is considering a plan to punish some members of the NATO alliance that President Trump thinks were unhelpful to the U.S. and Israel during the Iran war, according to administration officials cited by the WSJ. The proposal would involve moving U.S. troops out of NATO countries deemed unhelpful and stationing them in countries that were more supportive. (WSJ)

China's foreign ministry said it hoped the "relevant parties can grasp this chance at peace and bring the region back to stability as soon as possible" after the U.S. and Iran agreed to a ceasefire in the weeks-long Middle East war. (RTRS)

ENERGY CRISIS:

Analysts estimates that about a third of the Gulf region’s oil refineries have been damaged by airstrikes, a loss of capacity that “will take several months at least to repair once hostilities end.” (WSJ)

Taiwan's state refiner CPC and trader Glencore have chartered tankers to load Middle Eastern crude for Asia, while at least two Chinese vessels are heading to the Strait of Hormuz to exit the Gulf, a day after the ceasefire in the U.S.-Iran war. Taiwan said on the tanker, "If passage is possible within the next two weeks or so, it can come over". (RTRS)

Japan is considering a new release of about 20 days' worth of oil reserves as early as May, Kyodo reported on Thursday, amid uncertainty over the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz despite a U.S.-Iran ceasefire. It now has enough oil for 230 days in its reserves. (RTRS)

Japan’s Mitsui OSK Lines Ltd., one of the world’s largest shipping companies, said it would need to scrutinize details of a US-Iran ceasefire agreement and its implementation before allowing its vessels to test the Strait of Hormuz. (BBG)

Russia is seeking to leverage a global natural gas supply crunch to lure energy-starved South Asia into purchasing shipments from its US-sanctioned facilities, according to Bloomberg sources. (BBG)

US crude exports are projected to hit a record high in April as Asian customers hunt for supplies to replace Middle Eastern oil lost because of the Iran war. (FT)

China is considering financial relief and other measures for its struggling state-run airlines as the Iran war sends fuel costs soaring, according to Bloomberg sources, in what could be the industry’s biggest lifeline since the Covid pandemic. (BBG)

Governments that rushed to cut fuel taxes after the start of the Iran war must swiftly phase out costly universal energy subsidies, the OECD’s new chief economist said. (FT)

Brent crude is set to average more than $100 a barrel through 2026 if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed for another month, according to Goldman Sachs Group Inc. (BBG)

Britain has become the leading global destination for US exports of jet fuel as the aviation sector seeks to plug the gap left by the slowdown of deliveries from the Gulf since the start of the war in Iran, according to new data. (FT)

MACRO:

Bill Ackman is in talks to launch a strategy that would make big bets on complacency in financial markets, in a bid to mimic the success of doomsday trades the billionaire investor made during the pandemic. (FT)

The US administration plans to continue emphasizing its pro AI stance ahead of the midterms, emphasizing the importance of winning the tech race with China rather than address concerns about issues including job losses, White House officials said to the WSJ. (WSJ)

Wealthy investors attempted to pull more than $20bn from private credit funds in the first quarter, underscoring the growing strain on an asset class that had boomed into a dominant force on Wall Street. (FT)

Wall Street’s top regulators should investigate unusual trading activity in oil and equity futures markets shortly before President Donald Trump postponed military strikes against Iran last month, a lawmaker said Wednesday. (BBG)

Japan's consumer confidence worsened in March at a pace unseen since the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, a government survey showed, swelling the toll on a fragile economy from soaring fuel costs caused by the Middle East conflict. (RTRS)

Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said on Thursday real interest rates are clearly negative and keeping the country's financial conditions accommodative. (RTRS)

Japan’s five-year government bond auction Thursday drew demand that was largely in line with the 12-month average, after the temporary ceasefire in the Iran war provided some support. (BBG)

The Bank of Japan will probably increase its benchmark rate this month to avoid falling behind on controlling inflation, according to Masaaki Kaizuka, a former executive director at the central bank. (BBG)

Hedge funds are placing bets using currency options that the South Korean won and Chinese yuan will strengthen as risk sentiment improves and oil prices fall on news of the US-Iran ceasefire. (BBG)

As war injects extreme volatility into oil and gas markets, the global race for energy security is making China stronger, according to Jacky Tang, emerging markets chief investment officer at the private banking arm of Deutsche Bank AG. (BBG)

Chinese fund managers favor sectors like AI, innovative drugs and new energy as their investment theme on improving earnings and low valuations, China Securities Journal reports, citing fund management companies’ 2Q investment strategies. (China Securities Journal)

The EU will still be hit by a “stagflationary shock” of low growth and rising inflation despite the US and Iran agreeing a two-week ceasefire, the bloc’s top economic official has warned. (FT)

German industrial production declined unexpectedly in February, with the energy-price shock from the conflict in the Middle East expected to hamper output further. (WSJ)

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni vowed to stay on until the end of her government’s mandate, seeking to stabilize her tenure after a bruising referendum loss last month. (BBG)

The pound looks more vulnerable than the euro in options markets, a sign that traders see the UK as more exposed to a spike in energy prices even after the Iran ceasefire. (BBG)

Britain's housing market cooled noticeably last month as economic uncertainty stemming from the Iran war unnerved buyers who face rising mortgage rates, a RICS survey showed. (RTRS)

Australia’s pension funds have endured their worst monthly losses in more than three years as the war in Iran triggered market swings that battered some of their biggest investments. (BBG)

New Zealand’s recently appointed central bank governor, Anna Breman, warns that policymakers stand ready to raise interest rates forcefully if the Middle East crisis spills over into a sustained rise in inflation and expectations of higher prices. (WSJ)

The Korean won may rebound back to levels seen before the US-Iran war in the second quarter because of lower oil prices and foreign inflows to stocks, strategists said. (BBG)

Short covering was a key driver of India’s stock-market rebound on Wednesday, according to positioning data, pointing to a lack of conviction behind the biggest rally in almost a year. (BBG)

Thailand's central bank will keep its policy interest rate on hold, with economic growth projected at 1.3% to 1.7% this year, the central bank chief said on Thursday. (RTRS)

S&P Global Ratings lowered its outlook on the Philippines to stable from positive, saying the war in the Middle East has raised risks for the country’s balance of payments and fiscal position. (BBG)

The Dangote Group will need at least $40 billion of investment to fund a growth drive over the next five years that includes quadrupling fertilizer output and more than doubling its oil refinery capacity, the African Export-Import Bank said. (BBG)

Colombia’s credit score was downgraded by S&P Global Ratings for the second time in less than a year on concerns over a persistently large fiscal deficit and high debt burden. (BBG)

Venezuela’s interim government will raise monthly salaries for public-sector workers as authorities seek to ease pressure on households after months of high inflation and low wage increases. (BBG)

GEOPOLITICAL:

North Korea tested anew cluster-bomb warhead on a ballistic missile and an electromagnetic weapon this week, state media KCNA reported on Thursday, in a move seen as part of efforts by Pyongyang to showcase its capacity to fight a modern war. (RTRS)

Russia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs summoned Japanese ambassador to Moscow Akira Muto to lodge a protest over an investment agreement between Japan’s Terra Drone and a Ukrainian developer of unmanned aerial vehicles, according to a statement from the ministry. Warned that Russia-Japan relations had reached an all-time low. (BBG)

EQUITIES:

Anthropic employees have sold some equity to investors, wrapping up a secondary share sale that started earlier this year, according to Bloomberg sources. But some investors weren’t able to pick up as many shares as they planned because of the limited number that employees were willing to sell. (BBG)

Pacific Investment Management Co. is looking to sell a portion of the $14 billion of debt financing it’s providing for a massive Oracle Corp. data center in Michigan, according to Bloomberg sources. (BBG)

Rene Haas, the CEO of chip designer Arm, is in line to lead much of parent SoftBank's international business while keeping his current role at Arm, accoridng to the FT on Thursday, citing sources. (FT)

Disney is preparing to make sizable layoffs in one of the first significant moves under the new chief executive officer, Josh D’Amaro. (WSJ)

Constellation Brands logged lower revenue in its latest quarter as demand for its beer, wine and spirits remains weak. (WSJ)

Barrick Mining Corp. said it plans to reduce exposure to higher-risk jurisdictions and signaled openness to top-tier acquisitions, as it prepares to spin off its prized North American operations. (BBG)

A diesel hydrotreater and the control room for multiple hydrotreating units at Valero’s 380,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) Port Arthur, Texas, refinery were destroyed by a March 23 explosion and fire, according to Reuters sources. The refinery accounts for 3.7% of refining capacity in the U.S. (RTRS)

TSMC faces growing challenges as rivals court its engineers and supply chain partners, media report, with Elon Musk having already hired TSMC engineers for advanced packaging (FOPLP) and PCB work in Texas, and now for the TeraFab project. (DigiTimes via @dnystedt)

Seven & i Holdings Co. will delay a public listing of its US convenience-store business planned for later this year, saying it needs more time to turn the business around while navigating uncertain market conditions. (BBG)

The Japanese owner of clothing brand Uniqlo raised its full-year forecast on Thursday, flagging another record year, as international growth produced a stronger-than-expected jump in quarterly profit. (RTRS)

China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology will make forward-looking arrangements to steadily promote the development of the space computing power industry. (Xinhua via BBG)

France's OVHcloud is creating a dedicated defence unit after several European defence ministries approached it to support their military digital transformation, the datacentre operator said on Thursday. (RTRS)

Austrian oil and gas group OMV said on Thursday it expected higher energy prices to more than offset disruptions to production and sales volumes caused by the war in the Middle East. (RTRS)

🔥 WATCH NOW | Deep Blue Dialogue
The geopolitical chessboard is shifting, and Asia is right in the line of fire.

Our latest discussion dives deep into the Impact of the Middle East Conflict on U.S. Allies in Asia, with a sharp focus on the Philippines and the broader Indo-Pacific.

🌏 What’s at stake?
Part I: Strategic Shockwaves
- Is the U.S. facing strategic overstretch—and does this weaken its “Pivot to Asia”?

- Could tensions in the Middle East open dangerous gaps in the South China Sea?

- Are EDCA sites in the Philippines now potential targets in a widening conflict?

What happens if millions of OFWs are forced to return home overnight?

Part II: Testing the Alliance
- Can Washington still honor the Mutual Defense Treaty under pressure from multiple fronts?

- Are EDCA sites quietly evolving into launchpads for global U.S. operations—and at whose cost?

Part III: Economic & Regional Fallout
- Oil shocks are coming—can ASEAN act collectively, or will every state fend for itself?

- Will Manila rethink its posture and pursue de-escalation with China, or double down on alignment?

Part IV: Hard Questions for Policy
- Should the Philippines pursue strategic autonomy—or deeper entanglement?

If foreign bases become magnets for threats, will public support begin to crack?

⚠️ Bottom Line: This is no longer a distant war (Middle East War). The consequences are here, immediate, and deeply structural, from energy prices to national security, from foreign policy to domestic stability.
